title: The full sampler
goal:
Implement the reverse process of Section 2.4 on top of the two remasking steps. `lowconf_step` and `random_step` from the previous exercise are finished for you.

`generate(predict, length, steps, mask_id, remask="low_confidence", rng=None)` starts from a sequence of `length` masks. `predict(x)` returns logits of shape `(length, V)` for the current sequence `x`. At step $k = 1, \dots, N$ with $N$ = `steps`, call `predict` once, then apply one remasking step so that `length * k // steps` positions are unmasked afterward. This is $n_{un} = \lfloor L(1 - s) \rfloor$ at $s = 1 - k/N$, in integer arithmetic. Use `lowconf_step` for `"low_confidence"` and `random_step` for `"random"`, and raise `ValueError` for anything else. Return the final sequence.

The tests use a toy model with a fixed table of confidences, so you can compare the two strategies on the same model.
hints: Start with `x = np.full(length, mask_id)` and loop `for k in range(1, steps + 1)`.
Compute `n_un = length * k // steps` with integers. A float $1 - s$ can round just below an integer and drop one token.
Call `predict(x)` on the current sequence at every step, including steps after the first. The logits on a partly unmasked sequence differ from those on a fully masked one.
Pass `rng` through to `random_step` only. The low-confidence strategy is deterministic.
At the last step `n_un` equals `length`, so no position stays masked.
